holidays.name: Men Make Dinner Day
holidays.description: Aprons on, fellas. Today is the day for the men of the house to plan, cook and serve a whole dinner. They should also take on the dishes if they're feeling brave. It's a chance to show that a spatula isn't only for the grill.
holidays.origin: It's an unofficial observance, usually credited to a 1990s newspaper columnist who wanted to nudge men toward the stove. It has been marked on calendars every November 5 since.
holidays.funFact: The day is usually pitched as a way to give regular cooks a night off. Even a perfectly cooked box of mac and cheese counts as a heroic first step.

holidays.name: Guy Fawkes Night
holidays.description: Bonfires, fireworks, sparklers and toffee apples light up the British night. Effigies of Guy Fawkes, known as 'guys', are traditionally burned to mark a famously failed plot to blow up Parliament.
holidays.origin: On November 5, 1605, Guy Fawkes was caught guarding barrels of gunpowder under the House of Lords. The plot to kill King James I had failed. Parliament soon ordered a day of thanksgiving, and the bonfire tradition grew from it.
holidays.funFact: The 'guy' in the effigy gave English the word 'guy', which first meant a oddly dressed person and later any fellow.

holidays.name: Love Your Red Hair Day
holidays.description: A celebration of gingers, redheads and strawberry blondes. Redheads are encouraged to show off their fiery locks with pride. Everyone else is invited to admire them.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It is cheerfully embraced each year by redheads and fans of red hair.
holidays.funFact: Only about 1–2% of people worldwide have natural red hair. It comes from a variant of the MC1R gene.
